scope: Owned apply/fixed_apply control transfer, complete i_apply/i_apply_last/i_apply_only/apply/apply_last cases, and their three-register swap lowering.
adaptations: erlang:apply/3 is a code-space-owned instruction export, not a value-returning BIF or successful stub. Its real i_apply_only trampoline supports external-fun dispatch; compiler call forms retain complete native apply instruction cases and continuation/deallocation behavior.

Parse proper argument lists with the native 255-argument ceiling and error precedence; flatten exact nested apply/3 triples iteratively. Preserve the innermost triple for native badarg/system_limit. Precharge publication, resolve only an existing published exact export, acquire its code lease, then install arguments without any remaining fallible operation or collection.

Loaded module and admitted native/instruction targets are callable. Missing targets refuse the execution profile: no stub export, autoload, error_handler invocation, filesystem lookup or invented undef. Loading remains forbidden after execution starts. apply/2 remains outside this slice.

Installed OTP 28 (ERTS 16.3) parses 256/257 arguments, unlike pinned erl_vm.h MAX_ARG=255. The oracle records its badarg for a 256-cell improper list separately; the pinned native helper returns system_limit. Both reject 255-cell improper lists as badarg and 1024-cell lists as system_limit. This discrepancy is not hidden by claiming complete oracle equivalence.

Fixed apply validates initialized arguments plus module/function registers and reloads all movable values after constructing badarg argument lists with charged GC and preserved heap credit. Unsupported tracing/saved-call instrumentation is removed, not semantic instruction paths. Existing terminal exception handling is reused; full catch/unwind and trace reconstruction are not newly claimed.

Dynamic target modules use the existing process code-lease machinery; GC marks current PCs and stack continuations even when no fun term remains. Export-retain walks now also contribute their already-charged work to the caller's soft scheduling cost.

Compiler-produced fixtures and independent OTP evidence cover all five instruction cases, external apply export, loaded/native targets, nested calls, badarg and argument-ceiling precedence. Native tests exercise code PC/continuation leases, moving badarg roots, memory/callback allocation prefixes and every work prefix at helper and actual dispatch boundaries. Verifier tests reject missing MFA operands, excessive arity, wrong frames and stale post-call registers. Shared-worker tests verify exact bytes, budgets, safe reuse, peer survival and reclamation.
